symbols.name: \mathcal X
symbols.space: A finite set equipped with the discrete measurable structure.
symbols.def: \(\mathcal X\) is finite and carries the discrete \(\sigma\)-algebra \(2^{\mathcal X}\); in particular, every singleton \(\{x\}\) is measurable.

symbols.name: x^{\star}
symbols.role: The sole covariate cell in the three-level witness.

symbols.name: Y_0
symbols.role: Outcome under treatment zero when defined.

symbols.name: Y_1
symbols.role: Outcome under treatment one when defined.

symbols.name: P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\star}
symbols.def: The fully specified one-cell observed-data law in the three-level witness.

symbols.name: P^{\star}
symbols.def: The compatible full latent law explicitly allocated in the three-level witness.

symbols.name: P^L
symbols.def: The lower endpoint-attaining full law supplied by the full-law attainment theorem.

symbols.name: P^U
symbols.def: The upper endpoint-attaining full law supplied by the full-law attainment theorem.

symbols.name: d(x)
symbols.def: \(d:\mathcal X\to\{-1,+1\}\) indexes the weak selection-monotonicity direction among compliers in each covariate cell.
symbols.role: Latent cellwise direction, including cells on the observable tie face.

symbols.name: \Gamma_x^{0}
symbols.def: The complete fixed-marginal coupling polytope on the observable tie face.

symbols.name: \Gamma_x
symbols.def: The tie-safe partial-transport feasibility set selected by the sign of \(\Delta q(x)\), with a separate zero-gap branch.

symbols.name: B_L(x)
symbols.def: The lower threshold-cut value in cell \(x\).

symbols.name: B_U(x)
symbols.def: The upper threshold-cut value in cell \(x\).

symbols.name: \Theta_I(P_{\mathrm{obs}})
symbols.def: The identified set of \(\theta\) over compatible full laws.

symbols.name: \mathcal X_+(P)
symbols.role: Fixed positive-survivor support at a law \(P\).

symbols.name: \mathbb Z_{P_{\mathrm{obs}}}
symbols.def: The joint multinomial Gaussian limit of the finite vector of empirical observed-cell probabilities under \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\).

symbols.name: \mathcal A_L(x)
symbols.def: The set of threshold cuts attaining \(B_L(x)\), including the zero cut.

symbols.name: \mathcal A_U(x)
symbols.def: The set of threshold cuts attaining \(B_U(x)\), including the mass cap.

symbols.name: \widetilde\ell_i(x)
symbols.def: The empirical analogue of \(\ell_i(x)\), with every empirical conditional probability defined as zero when its empirical \(X,Z\) denominator is zero.

symbols.name: \widetilde h_j(x)
symbols.def: The empirical analogue of \(h_j(x)\), with every empirical conditional probability defined as zero when its empirical \(X,Z\) denominator is zero.

symbols.name: \widehat\ell_i(x)
symbols.def: The lower-arm coordinates of \(\widehat c_n\), equivalently \(\widehat\ell_i(x)=\max\{\widetilde\ell_i(x),0\}\).

symbols.name: \widehat h_j(x)
symbols.def: The higher-arm coordinates of \(\widehat c_n\), equivalently \(\widehat h_j(x)=\max\{\widetilde h_j(x),0\}\).

symbols.name: \widehat B_L(x)
symbols.def: The lower threshold-cut value obtained by substituting projected capacities into the positive, negative, or exact-zero branch according to the sign of \(\widehat{\Delta q}(x)\).

symbols.name: \widehat B_U(x)
symbols.def: The upper threshold-cut value obtained by substituting projected capacities into the positive, negative, or exact-zero branch according to the sign of \(\widehat{\Delta q}(x)\).

symbols.name: \widehat r_x
symbols.role: Unconditional estimated cell survivor mass used for screening.

symbols.name: \eta_n
symbols.def: A zero-cell omission threshold satisfying \(\eta_n\to0\) and \(\sqrt n\eta_n\to\infty\).

symbols.name: \widehat\Psi_n
symbols.def: \(\widehat\Psi_n=(\widehat N_{L,n}/\widehat M_n,\widehat N_{U,n}/\widehat M_n)\) when \(\widehat M_n>0\), and \(\widehat\Psi_n=(0,1)\) when \(\widehat M_n=0\).

symbols.name: \widehat{\mathcal A}_{L,n}(x;a_n)
symbols.def: The lower cuts within \(a_n\) of the estimated lower optimum.

symbols.name: \widehat{\mathcal A}_{U,n}(x;a_n)
symbols.def: The upper cuts within \(a_n\) of the estimated upper optimum.

symbols.name: \xi_r
symbols.def: A conditionally independent, mean-zero, unit-variance multiplier for observation \(r\).

symbols.name: \mathbb G_n^{\xi}
symbols.def: \(\mathbb G_n^{\xi}=n^{-1/2}\sum_{r=1}^n\xi_r\{\delta_{O_r}-\widehat P_n\}\) for conditionally mean-zero, unit-variance multipliers.

symbols.name: \mathcal C_{1-\alpha,n}
symbols.def: A simultaneous confidence set for the entire identified interval.

symbols.name: \mathcal M
symbols.def: The structural law class satisfying the maintained identification conditions, including tie-safe weak selection monotonicity but no direction-separation condition.
symbols.role: Domain for the sharp identified set.

symbols.name: \mathcal P_n
symbols.def: The triangular-array subclass of \(\mathcal M\) used only for estimation and uniform inference.

symbols.name: \Gamma_x^{\ast}
symbols.def: The branch-free exact-mass survivor-complier capacity polytope.

symbols.name: \mathcal E
symbols.type: finite collection of observable measurable events
symbols.def: \(\mathcal E=\bigl\{\{X=x\}:x\in\mathcal X\bigr\}\cup\bigl\{\{X=x,Z=z\}:x\in\mathcal X,\ z\in\{0,1\}\bigr\}\cup\bigl\{\{X=x,Z=z,D=d,S=1,Y=k\}:x\in\mathcal X,\ z,d\in\{0,1\},\ k\in\mathcal Y\bigr\}.\)
symbols.role: Finite event class controlling every empirical cell numerator and denominator.

symbols.name: \delta_n
symbols.role: Maximal empirical deviation over the finite guard event class.

symbols.name: A_{n,\alpha}
symbols.role: Capacity-estimation and screening error envelope on the finite-sample concentration event.

assumptions.condition: \(P\{d(x)(S_1-S_0)\ge0\mid C,X=x\}=1\) for every \(x\) with \(P(C\mid X=x)>0\), where \(d(x)\in\{-1,+1\}\).

standard.name: Covariate-specific weak sample-selection monotonicity of Dong and Heiler, Assumption 3.2

assumptions.condition: \(|\Delta q(x)|\ge\kappa_{\sigma}\) for every \(x\in\mathcal X\) with \(p_x>0\) and \(m(x)>0\).

standard.name: Strong sign-separation variant for covariate-specific selection direction

definitions.name: Tie-safe survivor-complier model
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M=\{P:P\text{ satisfies conditional instrument independence, treatment consistency, treatment-mediated selection and outcome exclusion, instrument overlap, no defiers, latent-direction weak selection monotonicity, and positive aggregate survivor-complier mass}\}\).  This is the finite-ordered, finite-covariate specialization of Dong--Heiler Assumptions 3.1--3.2 on cells with \(P(C\mid X=x)>0\); cells with \(P(C\mid X=x)=0\) have zero capacities and are inert for the target.

definitions.name: Margin-free uniform inference law class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal P_n=\{P\in\mathcal M:P\text{ satisfies the uniform aggregate-survivor and independent-sampling conditions at index }n\}\).  No selection-direction separation condition is imposed.

definitions.name: Observable selected-complier capacities
definitions.construction: For \(i,j\in\mathcal Y\), form \(\ell_i(x)\) and \(h_j(x)\) from the two conditional instrument contrasts displayed in the symbol table, set \(q_0(x)=\sum_i\ell_i(x)\), \(q_1(x)=\sum_jh_j(x)\), define \(\Delta q(x)=q_1(x)-q_0(x)\), and set \(m(x)=\min\{q_0(x),q_1(x)\}\).

definitions.name: Branch-free exact-mass partial-transport polytope
definitions.construction:
\[\Gamma_x^{\ast}=\left\{\gamma_x\ge0:\sum_j\gamma_{ij,x}\le\ell_i(x),\ \sum_i\gamma_{ij,x}\le h_j(x),\ \sum_{i,j}\gamma_{ij,x}=m(x)\right\}.\]
For comparison, retain
\[\Gamma_x^{+}=\left\{\gamma_x\ge0:\sum_j\gamma_{ij,x}=\ell_i(x),\ \sum_i\gamma_{ij,x}\le h_j(x)\right\},\qquad
\Gamma_x^{-}=\left\{\gamma_x\ge0:\sum_j\gamma_{ij,x}\le\ell_i(x),\ \sum_i\gamma_{ij,x}=h_j(x)\right\},\]
and
\[\Gamma_x^{0}=\left\{\gamma_x\ge0:\sum_j\gamma_{ij,x}=\ell_i(x),\ \sum_i\gamma_{ij,x}=h_j(x)\right\}.\]
Define \(\Gamma_x=\Gamma_x^{\ast}\).

definitions.name: Closed threshold-cut endpoints
definitions.construction:
For every \(x\in\mathcal X\), define
\[
B_L(x)=\max\left\{0,\ \max_{t\in\mathcal Y}\bigl[\ell_{\le t}(x)-h_{\le t}(x)\bigr]+\min\{\Delta q(x),0\}\right\}
\]
and
\[
B_U(x)=\min\left\{m(x),\ \min_{t\in\mathcal Y}\bigl[\ell_{<t}(x)+h_{>t}(x)\bigr]\right\}.
\]
These formulas are branch-free and remain defined on positive-survivor zero-gap cells and on zero-survivor cells.

definitions.name: Threshold-flow and latent-completion construction
definitions.construction: In each cell, first compute the exact mass \(m(x)\), the prefix and tail sums, and the two threshold values.  For an upper-attaining coupling, greedily construct a maximum subflow on the nested benefit graph \(i<j\); for a lower-attaining coupling, greedily construct a maximum subflow on the nested nonbenefit graph \(j\le i\).  Complete either subflow to total mass \(m(x)\) by a two-pointer allocation on the residual complete bipartite graph.  The result belongs to \(\Gamma_x^{\ast}\).  Allocate every row or column residual to the one-sided selected-complier stratum forced by the sign of \(q_1(x)-q_0(x)\), put the remaining compliers in the never-selected stratum, and adjoin the unchanged never-taker and always-taker components of a baseline compatible law.

definitions.name: Fully specified three-level observed and latent witness
definitions.construction: Let \(X=x^{\star}\) almost surely, \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\star}(Z=1)=P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\star}(Z=0)=1/2\), and \(K=3\). Given \(Z=0\), assign probabilities \(0.075\), \(0.10\), and \(0.075\) to \((D,S,Y)=(0,1,0),(0,1,1),(0,1,2)\), respectively, and probability \(0.75\) to \((D,S,Y)=(0,0,\star)\). Given \(Z=1\), assign probabilities \(0.10\), \(0.25\), and \(0.15\) to \((D,S,Y)=(1,1,0),(1,1,1),(1,1,2)\), respectively, and probability \(0.50\) to \((D,S,Y)=(1,0,\star)\); all unlisted conditional cells have probability zero. Construct \(P^{\star}\) by taking every unit to satisfy \(D_0=0,D_1=1\), allocating masses \(0.075,0.10,0.075\) to \(S_0=S_1=1\) with diagonal survivor pairs \((Y_0,Y_1)=(0,0),(1,1),(2,2)\), allocating mass \(0.25\) to \(S_0=0,S_1=1\) with \(Y_1\) residual masses \((0.025,0.15,0.075)\), and allocating mass \(0.50\) to \(S_0=S_1=0\). Take \(Z\) independent with probability one half and assign arbitrary latent outcomes wherever selection makes them unobserved.

definitions.name: Total constrained plug-in endpoint estimator
definitions.construction:
For every empirical conditional probability given \((X=x,Z=z)\), use its empirical ratio when the denominator is positive and the fixed value zero when the denominator is zero. Form \(\widetilde c_n=(\widetilde\ell,\widetilde h)\), set \(\mathfrak C=\prod_{x\in\mathcal X}\mathbb R_+^{2K}\), and define \(\widehat c_n=\Pi_{\mathfrak C}(\widetilde c_n)=\arg\min_{c\in\mathfrak C}\|c-\widetilde c_n\|_2^2\). The fixed Euclidean metric makes the minimizer unique, and \(\Pi_{\mathfrak C}\) is the coordinatewise positive-part map. From \(\widehat c_n=(\widehat\ell,\widehat h)\), form \(\widehat q_0(x)=\sum_i\widehat\ell_i(x)\), \(\widehat q_1(x)=\sum_j\widehat h_j(x)\), \(\widehat{\Delta q}(x)=\widehat q_1(x)-\widehat q_0(x)\), and \(\widehat m(x)=\min\{\widehat q_0(x),\widehat q_1(x)\}\). Evaluate
\[
\widehat B_L(x)=\max\left\{0,\ \max_{t\in\mathcal Y}\left[\sum_{i\le t}\widehat\ell_i(x)-\sum_{j\le t}\widehat h_j(x)\right]+\min\{\widehat{\Delta q}(x),0\}\right\}
\]
and
\[
\widehat B_U(x)=\min\left\{\widehat m(x),\ \min_{t\in\mathcal Y}\left[\sum_{i<t}\widehat\ell_i(x)+\sum_{j>t}\widehat h_j(x)\right]\right\}.
\]
Set \(\widehat r_x=\widehat p_x\widehat m(x)\), retain exactly the cells satisfying \(\widehat r_x>\eta_n\), and form \(\widehat M_n=\sum_x\mathbf 1\{\widehat r_x>\eta_n\}\widehat p_x\widehat m(x)\), \(\widehat N_{L,n}=\sum_x\mathbf 1\{\widehat r_x>\eta_n\}\widehat p_x\widehat B_L(x)\), and \(\widehat N_{U,n}=\sum_x\mathbf 1\{\widehat r_x>\eta_n\}\widehat p_x\widehat B_U(x)\). Define \(\widehat\Psi_n=(\widehat N_{L,n}/\widehat M_n,\widehat N_{U,n}/\widehat M_n)\) when \(\widehat M_n>0\), and use the fixed fallback \(\widehat\Psi_n=(0,1)\) otherwise.

definitions.name: Conservative guarded inference and face diagnostic
definitions.construction:
Use the same retained-cell rule \(\widehat r_x>\eta_n\).  The near-active lower and upper threshold cuts, the active face of \(\min\{\widehat{\Delta q}(x),0\}\), the active face of \(\min\{\widehat q_0(x),\widehat q_1(x)\}\), and the coordinatewise nonnegativity faces generated by \(\Pi_{\mathfrak C}\) define a computable finite diagnostic face envelope for \(\mathbb G_n^\xi\).  This multiplier envelope is not used as a calibrated critical value.  Retain \(a_n=(n\eta_n)^{-1/4}\) solely as its near-active-face localization tolerance.  The finite event collection \(\mathcal E\) and its maximal empirical deviation \(\delta_n\) supply the concentration input.  Set
\[
b_{n,\alpha}=\sqrt{\frac{|\mathcal E|}{4n\alpha}},\qquad
A_{n,\alpha}=\frac{64K|\mathcal X|}{\varepsilon_Z^2}b_{n,\alpha}+|\mathcal X|\eta_n,
\qquad
g_{n,\alpha}=\min\left\{1,\frac{4A_{n,\alpha}}{m_{\star}}\right\}.
\]
Define the conservative guarded confidence set
\[
\mathcal C_{1-\alpha,n}=
\left[\max\{0,\widehat\Psi_{n,L}-g_{n,\alpha}\},\
\min\{1,\widehat\Psi_{n,U}+g_{n,\alpha}\}\right].
\]
The alpha-indexed deterministic guard supplies finite-sample uniform containment and uniform endpoint consistency; first-order exact calibration of an unguarded face-aware multiplier region remains outside this construction.

statements.statement: For every supported \(x\in\mathcal X\) and \(i,j\in\mathcal Y\), \(\ell_i(x)=P(Y_0=i,S_0=1,C\mid X=x)\) and \(h_j(x)=P(Y_1=j,S_1=1,C\mid X=x)\). Hence \(\Delta q(x)=P(S_1=1,C\mid X=x)-P(S_0=1,C\mid X=x)\) and, under weak selection monotonicity, \(m(x)=P(S_0=S_1=1,C\mid X=x)\). If \(\Delta q(x)>0\), then \(d(x)=+1\); if \(\Delta q(x)<0\), then \(d(x)=-1\). No direction is identified from the observable gap when \(\Delta q(x)=0\).
statements.justification: This projection converts observed IV contrasts into the two latent submargins needed for transport.
statements.gap: KennedyHarrisKeele2019 targets a survivor-complier mean, and DongHeiler2026 Assumption 3.2 with equations (3.1)--(3.2) partitions weak selection directions for trimmed mean bounds; neither identifies the two ordinal submeasures as capacities for a same-unit coupling.
statements.consumer: An analyst can compute the survivor-complier outcome capacities directly from the Job Corps instrument, treatment, employment, and categorized-wage cells.

statements.statement: For every supported cell, \(\Gamma_x^{+}=\Gamma_x^{-}=\Gamma_x^{0}\) if and only if \(\Delta q(x)=0\). On this tie face, weak selection monotonicity implies \(P(S_0=S_1,C\mid X=x)=P(C\mid X=x)\), and \(\Gamma_x^{+}=\Gamma_x^{-}=\Gamma_x^{0}=\Gamma_x\): in \(\Gamma_x^{+}\), the column inequalities bind because their total capacity equals the required row mass, and symmetrically the row inequalities bind in \(\Gamma_x^{-}\). Moreover, \(\ell_{\le t}(x)-h_{\le t}(x)=h_{>t}(x)-\ell_{>t}(x)\) for every \(t\), so the increasing, decreasing, and explicit tie formulas for \(B_L(x)\) coincide, while all three branches share \(B_U(x)\).
statements.justification: The zero-gap face must be identified without assigning an artificial observable sign to a latent weak-monotonicity direction.
statements.gap: DongHeiler2026 equations (3.1)--(3.2) attach the no-selection intersection to one directional partition by convention; this proposition instead proves that the projected coupling geometry is direction-invariant exactly on that intersection.
statements.consumer: Implementations can evaluate zero selection-effect cells deterministically through the fixed-marginal branch and avoid an arbitrary sign convention.

statements.statement: For every \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\) compatible with \(\mathcal M\), the threshold-flow construction returns full laws \(P^L\) and \(P^U\) over \((Y_0,Y_1,S_0,S_1,D_0,D_1,X,Z)\) that belong to \(\mathcal M\), induce exactly \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}\), and obey \(P^L(Y_1>Y_0\mid S_1=S_0=1,C)=\theta_L\) and \(P^U(Y_1>Y_0\mid S_1=S_0=1,C)=\theta_U\), including observable tie cells and zero-survivor cells.
statements.justification: The exact-mass extremal couplings are pasted into full IV, compliance, and selection laws, closing the sharpness argument.
statements.gap: Projected coupling feasibility alone does not imply existence of a compatible full latent law.
statements.consumer: Simulation and sensitivity analyses can use exact least-favorable data-generating laws.

statements.statement: The displayed latent allocation defines \(P^{\star}\in\mathcal M\) and induces exactly the fully specified law \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\star}\): every unit is a complier, weak selection monotonicity holds in the increasing direction, and the selected cells under each instrument arm equal the listed probabilities. Applying the observable contrasts to \(P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\star}\) gives \(\ell=(0.075,0.10,0.075)\), \(h=(0.10,0.25,0.15)\), \(q_0=m=0.25\), \(q_1=0.50\), and \(\Delta q=0.25\). The threshold cuts then give \(B_L=0\) and \(B_U=0.175\); consequently the sharpness and full-law-attainment theorems imply \(\Theta_I(P_{\mathrm{obs}}^{\star})=[0,0.7]\) and attainment of both endpoints.
statements.justification: The witness separates survivor share, selected-arm mixture, and same-unit coupling uncertainty in the smallest informative ordered support.
statements.gap: ChenFlores2015 reports mean wage-effect bounds for always-employed Job Corps compliers, while deAguasEtAl2025 studies ordered-tier benefit from complete treatment-arm marginals; neither displays an IV-selection witness with unequal capacities and endpoint-attaining full laws.
statements.consumer: The witness is a reproducible diagnostic for software and a transparent calibration for the Job Corps reinterpretation.

statements.statement: On the no-selection submodel with \(P(S_0=S_1=1\mid C,X=x)=1\) for each cell with \(P(C\mid X=x)>0\), one has \(\Delta q(x)=0\) and \(\Gamma_x=\Gamma_x^{0}\), the full coupling polytope for the identified survivor-complier marginals \(\ell(x)/m(x)\) and \(h(x)/m(x)\). After division by \(m(x)\), \(B_L(x)\) and \(B_U(x)\) equal the sharp fixed-marginal strict-benefit formulas in LuDingDasgupta2018 Proposition 2, equation (6), cell by cell.
statements.justification: The reduction is the required sanity check that partial transport nests classical fixed-marginal benefit bounds.
statements.gap: LuDingDasgupta2018 Proposition 2, equation (6), establishes the complete-marginal formula; this theorem proves its exact equivalence to the \(\Gamma_x^{0}\) face recovered from the IV-selection model.
statements.consumer: Users can verify implementations against a published closed form whenever selection disappears.

statements.statement: Can the near-active-face directional-multiplier handle be calibrated so that \[\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{P\in\mathcal P_n}P\{\Theta_I(P_{\mathrm{obs}})\subseteq\mathcal C_{1-\alpha,n}\}\ge1-\alpha,\] uniformly over direction-separated triangular arrays \(\mathcal P_n\), while allowing arbitrary simultaneous threshold-cut ties and covariate cells whose survivor mass approaches zero and is omitted at the unnormalized threshold \(\eta_n\)?
statements.justification: Uniform simultaneous coverage at intersecting cut and zero-mass faces is the proposal's genuine unresolved inferential content.
statements.gap: FangSantos2019 handles estimated directional derivatives, ChernozhukovLeeRosen2013 handles localized contact sets, Semenova2025 handles covariate-specific Lee directions, and deAguasEtAl2025 equations (17)--(18) give pointwise stabilized coverage for tier-benefit bounds. None establishes uniform joint validity for two summed survivor-complier transport endpoints with changing cell support.
statements.consumer: The result would deliver an honest confidence set for the complete sharp Job Corps benefit interval even when several wage thresholds bind.

sampling_model.design: Binary conditionally randomized or conditionally exogenous instrument \(Z\), with observational receipt \(D\) and treatment-induced selection \(S\).
sampling_model.units: Independent draws \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) from a finite-cell superpopulation law.
sampling_model.treatment: Received treatment obeys \(D=D_Z\), no defiers, and exclusion through \(D\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Empirical finite-cell conditional probabilities use zero when an empirical \(X,Z\) denominator vanishes. Their raw IV contrasts are projected in the fixed Euclidean metric onto \(\mathfrak C=\prod_{x\in\mathcal X}\mathbb R_+^{2K}\), hence by coordinatewise positive part; cells are screened only through \(\widehat r_x=\widehat p_x\widehat m(x)>\eta_n\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Sharp bounds are derived for the survivor-complier average treatment effect under treatment-induced selection.
Bounds are derived for average wage effects among always-employed Job Corps compliers.
Assumptions 3.1--3.2 specify the IV, exclusion, no-defier, overlap, positive-first-stage, and cellwise weak selection-monotonicity structure for survivor-complier analysis.
comparator_promise_table.matched_by: The finite-ordered structural law class on positive-first-stage support

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Sharp lower and upper bounds are obtained for the probability that treatment is beneficial with fixed ordinal marginals.
Section 3.2, Theorem 2 and Results 3--4 give probability-of-benefit bounds under a distinct IV response-function model without treatment-induced survivor selection.

Definitions 1--2 and Propositions 4--5, equations (5)--(8), give ordered-tier benefit bounds from complete treatment-arm marginals under ignorability; Section 5 and Algorithm 1 address tied-bound nonregularity.
Derivative-estimated resampling is valid for directionally differentiable functionals where the ordinary bootstrap can fail.
Inference for intersection bounds is sharpened by localizing the set of binding indices.
Orthogonal inference is developed for Lee bounds with covariate-specific selection direction.
Lemma 2.1 gives pointwise-best-possible bounds for the distribution of \(Y_1-Y_0\) from identified complete potential-outcome marginals, with a conditional-covariate extension in Section 5.

A generic identification-and-estimation method gives sharp bounds on continuous functionals of joint potential-outcome distributions and permits unrestricted treatment assignment, instruments, and additional constraints.
Sharp probability-of-causation bounds are derived for always-observed units under exogenous treatment and monotone sample selection.

Under treatment unconfoundedness, monotonicity, and mean principal ignorability, principal generalized causal effects—including stratum-specific probabilistic-index and win-ratio estimands comparing potential outcomes for two randomly selected units in the same principal stratum—are point identified and estimated using U-statistics; the methods are illustrated using Job Corps.

tldr: Observed instrument contrasts identify two possibly unequal selected-complier outcome submeasures in each covariate cell. Latent-direction weak selection monotonicity makes their smaller total mass the survivor-complier mass; when the observable selection gap is zero, monotonicity forces selection equality among compliers and the two directional transport polytopes collapse to the same fixed-marginal tie face. Three-branch threshold cuts yield the sharp survivor-complier benefit interval, and a full-law construction attains both endpoints. A strongly polynomial algorithm, a fully specified compatible observed law with interval \([0,0.7]\), the classical fixed-marginal reduction, and a pointwise screened plug-in limit support the flagship identification result; uniform face-aware inference with changing survivor support remains open under a fixed direction margin.

project_justification.gap: DongHeiler2026 bounds survivor-complier means by trimming selected-complier distributions. LuDingDasgupta2018, GabrielSachsJensen2024, and deAguasEtAl2025 bound ordered benefit when complete treatment-arm marginals or different observable response-function restrictions are available. None characterizes the same-unit benefit probability from unequal survivor-complier submeasures induced jointly by noncompliance and treatment-dependent selection, including observable zero-gap cells.
project_justification.niche: Finite ordered outcomes make the strict-benefit graph a Ferrers network. Latent-direction weak selection monotonicity turns the two observed submeasures into row or column capacities off the zero-gap face and into complete survivor-complier marginals on the zero-gap face.
project_justification.fill: The project derives explicit increasing, decreasing, and tie branches; proves the sharp partial-transport interval and full IV-selection-law endpoint attainment; supplies a strongly polynomial algorithm and a compatible one-cell observed-law witness with interval \([0,0.7]\); recovers the Lu--Ding--Dasgupta formula on \(\Gamma_x^{0}\); defines a total screened plug-in estimator and its fixed-law directional limit; and isolates uniform face-aware multiplier validity as an open question.

related_work: KennedyHarrisKeele2019 establishes survivor-complier mean effects under treatment-induced selection and provides the principal-stratum framing. ChenFlores2015 bounds mean wage effects for always-employed Job Corps compliers; the fully specified compatible witness here calibrates instead the fraction whose ordered wage category rises. DongHeiler2026 Assumption 3.2 states cellwise weak sample-selection monotonicity, and equations (3.1)--(3.2) separate positive and negative direction cells while attaching the no-selection intersection to the positive partition by convention. Its sharp results concern intensive-margin means, so it informs the model but is not a theorem-level result being tightened. LuDingDasgupta2018 Proposition 2, equation (6), gives the sharp strict-benefit interval from two complete ordinal marginals; the no-selection theorem makes that formula exactly the \(\Gamma_x^{0}\) branch. GabrielSachsJensen2024 Section 3.2, Theorem 2 and Results 3--4 derive probability-of-benefit bounds under confounding and imperfect randomization by symbolic response-function methods, without treatment-induced survivor selection. deAguasEtAl2025 Definitions 1--2 define the same ordered-tier benefit event, Propositions 4--5 and equations (5)--(8) give sharp bounds from complete treatment-arm marginals under ignorability, and Section 5 with Algorithm 1 and equations (17)--(18) addresses nonregularity from tied complete-marginal bounds. That paper does not recover unequal survivor-complier submeasures under noncompliance and treatment-induced selection, derive directional partial-transport threshold formulas, or lift endpoint couplings to a compatible full IV-selection law. FangSantos2019 supplies directional resampling, ChernozhukovLeeRosen2013 supplies contact-set localization, and Semenova2025 studies covariate-specific Lee-bound directions; these sources motivate the fixed-law directional calculation and the separate open problem of uniform inference with estimated faces and changing survivor support.
technical_internal_limitation: Finite enumeration is evidence, not a proof. The early kill test enumerated denominator-five three-level capacity laws and solved the complier selection-type linear program with an explicit one-sided residual stratum. The linear-program endpoints agreed with the threshold formulas on 1,918 increasing-selection and 1,918 decreasing-selection laws, including 1,622 direction-specific checks on equal-total tie cases. The fully specified witness has an explicit compatible latent allocation and returns benefit masses \(0\) and \(0.175\), hence conditional endpoints \(0\) and \(0.7\). The general theorem still requires a symbolic endpoint-preserving completion for every compatible observed law. The pointwise directional limit does not by itself validate a confidence set.
honest_scope: The tie-safe capacity projection, three-branch threshold min-cut equality, full-law endpoint attainment, strongly polynomial construction, compatible three-level observed-law witness, fixed-marginal reduction, and fixed-law pointwise directional limit are theorem targets. Identification allows \(\Delta q(x)=0\) and \(m(x)=0\) and uses no direction margin. The pointwise limit imposes \(|\Delta q(x)|\ge\kappa_{\sigma}\) only on the fixed positive-survivor support and screens zero-survivor cells with probability tending to one. Uniform coverage with simultaneous cut ties, estimated near-active faces, and changing survivor support is explicitly open; rates for \(a_n\) and \(\eta_n\), critical-value calibration, uniform face recovery, and local-to-zero direction gaps are strengthening questions. No confidence-set validity, uniform inference, changing-support limit, or coverage under shrinking direction gaps is claimed. Continuous outcomes, monotonicity-violation sensitivity, and concordance restrictions are outside scope.
